name: net-snmp
desc: Implements SNMP v1, v2c, and v3, using IPv4 and IPv6
why: SNMP is a protocol running quietly on countless routers and printers, and net-snmp is a direct door into it.

brief.what_it_is: Net-SNMP is a suite of command-line tools, a graphical MIB browser, a trap receiver daemon, an extensible SNMP agent daemon, and a C and Perl library for building SNMP applications. It implements SNMP v1, v2c and v3 over both IPv4 and IPv6. The command-line tools send requests to SNMP-capable devices (routers, computers, UPSs) and read or set their management data, and the tools also translate between numeric and textual MIB OIDs. The trap daemon takes incoming SNMP notifications and logs them to syslog, the NT Event Log or a text file, forwards them to another management system, or passes them to an external program. The agent daemon answers SNMP queries and can be extended with loadable modules, external scripts, SMUX or AgentX. The homepage lists the current release as 5.9.4.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames SNMP as a widely used protocol for monitoring the health and welfare of network equipment, computer equipment and devices like UPSs, and presents Net-SNMP as the suite that implements it. The page gives no separate statement of motivation.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals. It describes the parts as separate programs: request tools such as snmpget, snmpwalk and snmpset, a trap receiver (snmptrapd), an extensible agent (snmpd), and a shared library with C and Perl APIs. The homepage does not describe how these parts communicate beyond the protocols they implement.
brief.install_notes: The homepage points to a Download section with source code and binaries for many Unix and Unix-like systems and for Microsoft Windows. It says to read the platform-specific README files, and the Tk/Perl-based MIB browser (tkmib) needs Tk and Perl. I did not open the download or documentation pages, so I have no first-run or configuration steps.
brief.standout: The suite covers both ends of SNMP in one package: the polling tools, the trap receiver and an agent you can extend with scripts or loadable modules. The agent also supports the older SMUX and newer AgentX extension protocols.
brief.status: Maintained, by the evidence I have. The homepage shows current release 5.9.4 and a last-modified date of 23-Dec-2025. The page says bugs and patches go through a GitHub project. I did not check the GitHub repository or the release history, so the release date of 5.9.4 is unverified.
brief.caveats: The homepage warns that functionality varies by operating system and says to check the platform README files. The MIB browser depends on Tk and Perl. I did not read the License page, so I cannot state the license. The executables list from the package metadata includes many more programs than the homepage names, and I did not verify each one.

judge.reason: Net-SNMP opens a hands-on window into the quietly ubiquitous SNMP protocol, letting you inspect and control devices and even build extensible agents.

entry.title: Net-SNMP
entry.tldr: The reference toolkit for SNMP, the protocol routers, printers and UPSs use to report their state: query devices, receive traps, or run your own agent.
entry.deeper_look:
Net-SNMP is a suite of command-line tools, a trap receiver daemon, an extensible agent daemon, a Tk/Perl MIB browser, and C and Perl libraries. It implements SNMP v1, v2c and v3 over IPv4 and IPv6. The request tools such as `snmpget`, `snmpwalk` and `snmpset` talk to a device and read or change its management data. Other tools translate between numeric OIDs and their textual MIB names.

SNMP is, in the homepage's words, "a widely used protocol for monitoring the health and welfare of network equipment (eg. routers), computer equipment and even devices like UPSs." It runs quietly on a huge amount of hardware, and most people never see it. This suite is a way to look at what those devices are willing to say about themselves.

The package covers both ends of the conversation. `snmptrapd` receives notifications and can log them to syslog or a text file, forward them elsewhere, or hand them to an external program. `snmpd` is an agent that answers queries, so your own machine can become something SNMP can ask questions of. It can be extended with loadable modules, external scripts, SMUX or AgentX.

The idea underneath is the MIB: a shared, tree-shaped naming scheme where every measurable thing on a device has a numeric address. Learning to walk that tree is learning how network monitoring systems see the world.
entry.install:
brew install net-snmp
# The MIB browser (tkmib) needs Tk and Perl. Querying a device needs one that speaks SNMP, or you can run snmpd locally.

try_this.what_happens: Shows the options for fetching a single value from an SNMP device, the simplest request the suite makes.
Shows how to walk a device's whole tree of management data, the usual way to see what it exposes.
Shows how to convert between numeric OIDs and readable MIB names, a good first look at the naming tree.

entry.whats_unique: It is both halves of SNMP in one package: the polling tools, the trap receiver and an agent you can extend with scripts or modules. It also supports both the older SMUX and newer AgentX extension protocols.
entry.caveats: The homepage warns that functionality varies by operating system, and the MIB browser needs Tk and Perl.
